subject: Hosted API latency thresholds — commitment draft & evidence checklist
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@novahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API latency thresholds — commitment draft & evidence checklist

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to hear more about NovaHealth’s real-time triage use case. As promised, I put together a short draft of the latency commitment we can offer for the hosted API and an evidence checklist you can use during procurement. This is a starting point for negotiation; we expect to adjust wording around maintenance windows and temporary migrations.

Proposed latency commitments (US region, production traffic):
- p50: <= 100 ms
- p95: <= 400 ms
- Measurement approach: 5-minute rolling buckets per request type, daily aggregation, 30-day lookback for contractual reporting

Key carveouts and operational notes:
- Planned maintenance windows (scheduled >48 hours notice) excluded from SLA calculation
- Short-term platform migration events (defined window, agreed in advance) can be excluded if mutually agreed and documented
- We include automatic fallback to a compatible model variant in the event of capacity constraints; fallback latency will be separately reported

Attached: SLO-Evidence-Checklist.pdf (lists logs, traces, and sample payloads we'll need for audit) and a draft amendment for your procurement team.

Ask: Can you confirm whether the measurement approach above maps to NovaHealth’s internal reporting (you mentioned daily SRE summaries) and whether the 30-day lookback is acceptable for audit purposes? Also flag any specific regional constraints we should be aware of.

If it helps I can loop in our SRE (Ben) and Legal (Marissa) for carveout language.

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@novahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: NovaHealth SRE Team <ops@novahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency thresholds — commitment draft & evidence checklist

Jonas,

Thanks for the clear summary. The numbers you suggested are in the right ballpark for us; a couple of follow-ups from the SRE/procurement side: 

- Measurement: We currently publish SRE reports using 1-minute windows; would the 5-minute rolling buckets obscure short, frequent spikes our oncall cares about? Would you be able to provide both 1-minute and 5-minute telemetry for the first 90 days to validate the aggregation approach?
- Maintenance carveouts: we can accept planned maintenance exclusion, but need the definition (duration, how you notify us).
- Uptime: our procurement team will want to tie latency to an availability commitment — can Redwood confirm a target uptime (e.g., 99.95%) for the hosted API during the same measurement period?

Also: we have a planned internal migration the week of Nov 8 that will cause elevated request volume and some traffic replays. Is there a standard temporary exception you offer for customer-side migrations, and what evidence would you require to exclude that window from SLA calculations?

Appreciate that you attached the checklist — I’ll share with procurement. If you can include the 1-minute telemetry option and draft language for a migration exception, that would speed review.

Best,
Emily Chen
SRE Lead, NovaHealth
emily.chen@novahealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Hosted API latency thresholds — commitment draft & evidence checklist

Jonas / Ben —

Looping in a short internal note after reviewing Emily’s asks. Procurement will push on: uptime linkage, explicit definitions for maintenance/migration exceptions, and dual-window telemetry. From Legal/procurement perspective we should: 

- Offer both 1-minute and 5-minute telemetry for the first 90 days for validation; contractual measurement can default to 5-minute buckets after validation period
- Define maintenance notification as: >48 hours advance notice via email to procurement contact + posting in status.redwood.ai; exclude windows with agreed start/end times
- For customer migration exceptions: require a joint migration plan (email thread with times and replay indicators) and a short post-mortem; limit exception to a single contiguous window up to 72 hours per migration event unless mutually extended
- Uptime: Legal prefers we avoid hard 99.95% availability language tied to latency percentiles unless we can quantify credits reliably. Suggest offering a draft uptime target in the amendment for negotiation but expose the credit rubric only after SRE sign-off.

Ben — can you confirm we can emit 1-minute telemetry and a 90-day validation retention? Also, please prepare the evidence checklist items Jon attached into a short packet we can hand to procurement (logs, sample traces, KV cache snapshots, region-specific request breakdown).

If all good, I recommend we propose the draft amendment with those bullets as negotiable items and offer a 30-day pilot to validate the measurements.

Marissa
VP Legal & Policy, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Hosted API latency thresholds — commitment draft & evidence checklist

Emily,

Thanks — appreciate the prompt feedback. Quick summary & next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Agreed next items:
- Redwood will provide both 1-minute and 5-minute telemetry for the first 90 days to validate aggregation. Contractual measurement will default to 5-minute rolling buckets after the validation period unless NovaHealth requests otherwise in writing.
- Maintenance: planned maintenance will be excluded if we provide >48 hours notice to the procurement contact and post to status.redwood.ai with start/end times.
- Migration exception: Redwood will allow a one-time migration exclusion up to 72 contiguous hours provided NovaHealth sends a joint migration plan (time windows, expected replay volume) and we receive a short post-mortem within 7 days. Extensions possible by mutual agreement.
- Uptime/credits: We will include a proposed availability target in the draft amendment, but the exact credit formula will be finalized after SRE sign-off.

I attached an updated draft amendment (proposed-sla-amendment-20261022.docx) and the SLO-Evidence-Checklist.pdf. Ben has confirmed we can emit 1-minute telemetry and retain the 90-day validation traces; Marissa has approved the proposed carveout language for migration events.

Can you confirm if procurement needs the HubSpot deal link or any additional company paperwork to speed signature? If Nov 8 migration is still on your calendar, if you can share the migration plan by Oct 29 we’ll slot the exclusion window into our reporting and coordinate sensor flags on our side.

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call with procurement and your SRE team if that helps close faster.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
